what: O5 §七 compiled-body audit of the target-source candidate. Program evidence settles contents and absences; runtime probes settle finiteness and variance. Neither alone is enough -- O4A is the reason.

candidateVsControlProgramBytes.note: The candidate's whole body -- refraction, dispersion, environment, rim, silhouette -- compiles to less than half the control's program, because it has no scene-colour path, no blur chain, no adaptive shaping and no debug branches.

runtimeProbe.unitLengthFractionNote: Not 100%, and should not be: 8-bit quantisation alone moves |N| by up to ~0.01, and the encoding clips any component beyond [-1,1]. What matters is that the distribution sits AT 1 rather than at 0, which is the O4A discriminator.

textureBindings.note: Both lanes bind two textures. The candidate's are its own media and the environment; the control's are the scene-colour target and the environment. Identifiers are minified, so which is which is settled by item 9's runtime proof, not by reading names.

items.name: analytic normal is finite
items.detail: 634495 card pixels read from the linear analytic-normal view; non-finite 0, all-black 0. Decoded |N| mean 1.0342 (p1 0.991, p99 1.7049).

items.name: NaN count = 0
items.detail: A NaN reaching the framebuffer clamps to 0 in an 8-bit target, so this is read together with item 1's all-black count rather than from the float alone: 0 non-finite AND 0 all-black card pixels.

items.name: Inf count = 0
items.detail: An Inf saturates to 255 across the board; channel maxima are [248.0, 248.0, 255.0] with real spread (std [46.94, 46.119, 46.619]), not a saturated plane.

items.name: normal has spatial variance
items.detail: Per-channel standard deviation across the card is [46.94, 46.119, 46.619]. This is the discriminator O4A turned on: a zero or constant normal reads as std 0.

items.name: Beauty refract consumes the analytic normal
items.detail: 5 refract() calls in the high program, and NO shared normal varying is declared at all (v_o*NormalView / normalViewGeometry: absent). The normal is computed per fragment from positionLocal, so there is nothing for refract to consume except the analytic normal.

items.name: every spectral sample executes its own refract
items.detail: refract() appears 5 times at high with 5 samples; 3 times at low with 3. The count tracks the sample count exactly, which is what distinguishes five real refractions from one refraction reused with UV offsets.

items.name: no zero-initialised shared normal alias reaches Beauty
items.detail: The O4A defect needs a shared varying to occur on. This program declares none, and has no debug branches at all -- each view is a separate program. The failure mode has no surface here.

items.name: own media texture is sampled
items.detail: 6 textureSample() calls -- at least one per spectral sample plus the environment. The media binding is the card's own VideoTexture; the lane creates its own textures and never mutates the control lane's reel textures.

items.name: scene-colour texture is not referenced
items.detail: Decisive runtime proof rather than a string search: in the candidate lane the scene-colour pass draws 0 calls and the media plane is hidden (0 visible of 100 active slots, 16 bodies drawn) -- yet the cards still show media, luminance std 80.795 inside the card. Nothing was ever rendered INTO the scene-colour target, so the media the body displays cannot have come from it. (A WGSL string search cannot settle this: identifiers are minified, and both lanes declare exactly two texture bindings -- the candidate's are its own media and the environment, the control's are the scene-colour target and the environment.)

items.name: no .level() / mip LOD path
items.detail: Candidate explicit-LOD sampler calls: none. Control program, as a POSITIVE control on the same test: {'textureSampleLevel': 20}. The probe demonstrably fires on a program that has the path, so the candidate's zero is an absence and not a broken check. Structurally reinforced: the lane's textures are created with generateMipmaps = false, so there is no chain to sample even if a LOD were requested.

items.name: no adaptive shaping nodes
items.detail: Adaptive-shaping identifiers in the candidate: none. The Target's factory contains none either (contract absence claims noAdaptiveContrast, noEdgeLift, noInternalShadow).

items.name: no ACES / tone-mapped body path
items.detail: Tone-mapping identifiers inside the body program: none. The material sets toneMapped=false exactly as the Target does. Note the flag is INERT under three's WebGPU node renderer in BOTH codebases -- 0 reads in our three.webgpu.js, and all 4 in the Target's bundle are WebGL-only paths -- so the renderer's output stage is left alone rather than overridden, which is what reproduces the Target's actual behaviour.

items.name: reflection and refraction use the same analytic normal
items.detail: Structural: the body chain computes N once into a var and both the spectral loop and the reflection vector read that same var. There is no second normal source in the program -- no varying, no vertex normal, no attribute.

items.name: high / medium / low all satisfy the contract
sample-count quality cap matches Target source
items.detail: Measured {'high': 5, 'medium': 5, 'low': 3}. The Target caps at min(dispersionSamples=5, low ? 3 : Infinity) -> 5 high / 3 low. We have three levels against its two, so medium maps to 5 and low to 3; recorded in o5-architecture.json as a stated 3-tier-to-2-tier mapping, not a transcription.

finalStateIfFailed: O5 TARGET-SOURCE BODY FAILED ABSOLUTE GATE
